title: Perfect tensor direct image over a Noetherian algebraic space
statement: Work with a scheme $S$ [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces over $S$ and their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], quasi-coherent modules [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], and the canonical module functors [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Derived pullback and tensor are computed with K-flat resolutions with flat terms, and derived direct image with K-injective resolutions. Perfect means etale locally isomorphic in the derived category to a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free structure modules. Finite presentation of a morphism means quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally finitely presented on etale scheme charts. A module is finitely presented when it locally has a presentation $\mathcal O^m\to\mathcal O^n\to M\to0$ with $m,n$ finite. Flatness over a base is flatness of geometric stalks over its corresponding geometric local rings. Proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed; the scheme theoretic support of a finitely presented module is the closed subspace cut out by its annihilator. Let $B$ be a Noetherian algebraic space, meaning quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally Noetherian on etale scheme charts. Let $f:X\to B$ be locally of finite type and quasi-separated, with no properness hypothesis on $f$. Let $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ be perfect. Let $G^\bullet$ be a bounded complex of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules, where coherent means quasi-coherent and finitely generated on the Noetherian affine etale charts of $X$. Assume each term is flat over $B$ and its scheme theoretic support is proper over $B$. Then $Rf_*(E\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_X}G^\bullet)$ is perfect in $D(\mathcal O_B)$.

proof.text: Fix $c\le d$ with $G^q=0$ for $q\notin[c,d]$, also when $G=0$. First $X$ is locally Noetherian: on compatible affine etale source and target charts, the source ring is a finite-type algebra over a Noetherian ring, hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Such charts cover $X$ by the chartwise meaning of locally finite type. Let $T_q=\operatorname{Supp}(G^q)$, the set of points with nonzero geometric stalk, and $T=\bigcup_{q=c}^dT_q$. Each $T_q$ is closed by [lem-sfb-space-noetherian-coherent-support], applied to the coherent $G^q$ and its zero submodule. Let $Z_q$ be the assumed proper scheme theoretic support, cut out by $\operatorname{Ann}(G^q)$. Then $T_q\subseteq|Z_q|$: if a geometric point $\bar x$ lies outside $|Z_q|$, choose an affine etale chart $\operatorname{Spec}A$ through it, on which $Z_q$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ with $I$ the annihilator ideal; the image prime $\mathfrak p$ of $\bar x$ does not contain $I$, so some $a\in I$ is a unit of $A_{\mathfrak p}$ and hence of the geometric local ring, while $a$ kills every local section of $G^q$ and so kills $G^q_{\bar x}$; thus $G^q_{\bar x}=0$. By [lem-sfb-space-proper-support-closed-operations], $|Z_q|$ is proper over $B$ (it carries the proper closed structure $Z_q$), hence so is its closed subset $T_q$, and the finite union $T$ is closed and proper over $B$. In particular $T$ is quasi-compact: its proper reduced subspace is quasi-compact over the quasi-compact $B$.

proof.text: Put $H=E\otimes^{\mathbf L}G^\bullet$. Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-strict-perfect-relative-tensor] on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ with $A=\mathcal O_X$ and $R=f^{-1}\mathcal O_B$; the geometric points are conservative by [lem-sfb-space-etale-conservative-geometric-points]. The assumed geometric-stalk flatness is exactly its flatness hypothesis. On each strict-perfect chart $U$ for $E$, with model interval $[a_U,b_U]$, it identifies $H|_U$ with the bounded total tensor $T_U^\bullet$. A term is a finite sum of retracts of finite sums of $G^q|_U$. Finite sums are coherent by [lem-sfb-space-coherent-abelian]; a retract is the image of its idempotent, hence a kernel followed by a cokernel of coherent modules, so is coherent by that same node. Taking kernels and cokernels of the differentials shows that every $H^i(H)|_U$ is coherent. Each $H^i(H)$ is quasi-coherent, since quasi-coherence is local on the site and holds on every $U$. The strict-perfect charts $U$ are etale schemes covering $X$, so their disjoint union $p:\coprod U\to X$ is a surjective etale scheme atlas, and $p^*H^i(H)$ is coherent because it is so on each summand. By the last clause of [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-groupoid-equivalence] on the locally Noetherian $X$, every $H^i(H)$ is coherent.

The chart images are open by [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image]. Their cover of the quasi-compact $T$ has a finite subcover $U_1,\ldots,U_N$. Put $r=\min_j(a_{U_j}+c)$ and $s=\max_j(b_{U_j}+d)$, choosing $r=s=0$ if $T$ is empty. The tensor-model bounds give $H^i(H)=0$ on these charts for $i\notin[r,s]$. On $X\setminus T$ the complex $G$ is zero, and the same local tensor calculation gives $H=0$. For any $R$-module sheaf $F$, the final isomorphism of [lem-sfb-ringed-strict-perfect-relative-tensor] gives these same bounds for $H\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}F[0]$ on every $U_j$. On the complement it gives zero, using $M=0$ on each strict-perfect chart there. These are a jointly surjective family of etale charts together with the complement. Exact conservative stalks [lem-sfb-space-etale-conservative-geometric-points] detect both vanishing assertions globally. Thus $H$ is bounded and its scalar restriction has the single Tor interval $[r,s]$, independent of $F$.

For each $i$, the coherent module $H^i(H)$ has closed geometric-stalk support by [lem-sfb-space-noetherian-coherent-support], applied to $F=H^i(H)$ and its zero quasi-coherent submodule. It is contained in $T$, since the local tensor models are zero on $X\setminus T$. Therefore [lem-sfb-space-proper-support-closed-operations] makes this support proper over $B$. This does not infer properness of $f$.

Apply [lem-sfb-space-bounded-coherent-finite-tor-image-perfect] to $f:X\to B$ and $H$. Its base is the given Noetherian algebraic space, and its morphism hypotheses are exactly the given local finite type and quasi-separatedness. Steps 2 and 3 give bounded coherent cohomology, step 4 gives proper cohomology supports, and step 3 gives finite Tor dimension over $f^{-1}\mathcal O_B$. Its conclusion is that $Rf_*H=Rf_*(E\otimes^{\mathbf L}G^\bullet)$ is perfect, as required.

The item statement is unchanged and matches 0DKJ; it is still unsplit live, so no other group has superseded it. The three new nodes are true and are not duplicates. The 08IS node is the space version of the scheme node lem-pc-bounded-coherent-finite-tor-proper-pushforward-perfect (08EV). The proper-support node states 0CZC, 0CZE and 0CZH with the lft hypothesis kept. The tensor node is a site generalization of the scheme and Zariski models (via 0E8K, 06YQ and stalkwise flatness). None of them restates a clause of the item. Fixes: (1) C1, step 1: the claim that T_q equals the point set of the scheme-theoretic support (07U0(4)/0CZI) was uncited, and closedness of T_q was uncited. Now T_q is closed by lem-sfb-space-noetherian-coherent-support, the inclusion T_q ⊆ |Z_q| is written out (some a in Ann is a unit in the geometric local ring and kills the stalk), and the proper-support node then gives that T_q and T are proper. The unneeded annihilator-support claim in step 4 is removed. (2) C1, step 2: 'coherence is local by definition' was wrong, because coherence must hold on every étale chart. Now the step cites the last clause of lem-sfb-space-qcoh-groupoid-equivalence for the atlas ∐U→X; I checked there is no cycle. (3) B3: the 08IS node now defines 'reduced induced closed subspace' inline. Steps 3 and 5 are correct: a finite chart subcover of the quasi-compact T gives a uniform interval, and H=0 off T.
